summary: Iteration 35: tested the new co-owners-and-managers scope feature (owner invites a manager restricted to specific projects). Backend 15/15 pytest passed covering invite validation (400 empty list, 404 bad pid, 404 project-not-owned-by-inviter, 400 duplicate invite), role/project_names in POST/PUT/GET responses, email_sent flag, shared-with-me role+count, manager data access (only picked project appears as shared, cannot activate others, activating allowed project returns 200 and /api/project, /api/line-items & /api/rentals work on allowed project), scope-change auto-switches active project, /api/portfolio/map and /api/portfolio/rent-roll exclude non-allowed projects, removal falls back to invitee's own projects, and full co-owner (null project_ids) sees every owner project. Frontend /co-owners screen loads via testID co-owners-screen; invite-role-co-owner / invite-role-manager chips toggle correctly, selecting Manager reveals invite-project-picker, button text switches to 'Make manager' vs 'Make co-owner', and co-owner-invite-button is disabled until both a valid email and (for manager) at least one project is picked.
critical_code_review_comments: co_owners.py `_check_pids` correctly dedupes, 400s empty list, and 404s project not owned by the inviter.

deps.effective() for managers filters allowed project_ids against still-existing projects owned by the acting owner and auto-switches `active_project_id` to the first allowed when the current one no longer qualifies, then persists it (good).
If a manager's access is revoked, effective() falls back to their own projects and clears acting_owner_id/active_project_id (good — tested).

projects.access_filter() returns a $or over own + full-co-owner owners + explicit project ids for managers, which is reused by /portfolio/map, /portfolio/rent-roll (via accessible_projects), activate_project, and shared_with_me count — single source of truth (good).
co_owners.py imports ObjectId directly from bson in /shared-with-me instead of using the project's `oid()` helper used elsewhere; mild inconsistency but fine (both validate IDs the same way).
`_out` performs 2 DB round-trips per co-owner row (users.find_one + projects.find). With MAX_CO_OWNERS=10 that's fine, but if the limit ever grows consider batching users and projects lookups.
Front-end: invite-project-picker test id is on the container; checkbox items use invite-project-{pid} and edit-project-{cid}-{pid} prefixes — all consistent with the request spec.

success_rate.frontend: Verified: role chips, project picker visibility, invite button disabled/enabled states, button-label switches; existing co-owner card edit flow verified structurally (demo had no co-owners live during UI run after cleanup)

seed_data_creation: During pytest a TEST_iter35 invitee user, a TEST_iter35 'other owner' user, and (only if the demo owner had just 1 project) a TEST_iter35_Scope_<hex> second project were created. All removed in teardown; demo owner's original project is reactivated at the end (test_zz_cleanup_demo_active).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run test_iteration35.py with `-o addopts=` to disable xdist — state flows across test classes (invite created in TestInviteAndScope is reused by TestManagerAccess & TestFullCoOwner). Env: EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL in /app/frontend/.env (not EXPO_BACKEND_URL). Login testIDs: auth-email-input, auth-password-input, auth-submit-button. The /co-owners route is accessible directly (Expo Router) but the auth token in web storage sometimes 401s after a hard refresh in Playwright; drive via /login first if you need the data queries to populate. On the UI, picker container itself is `invite-project-picker` and item ids are `invite-project-{pid}` — don't confuse the two when counting checkboxes.
rca_of_issue: No bugs discovered. All feature requirements from the request are implemented correctly.
